name: BASRA
description: Basra is the most popular card game in Egypt and widely played throughout the Levant. It is a 'Fishing' game related to Italian Casino, where players capture cards from a central pool by matching ranks or summing values. The game is named after the 'Basra' (or 'Basra Bonus'), awarded when a player clears the entire table with a single card. With simple math and high-stakes capturing mechanics (including the powerful Jack and 7 of Diamonds), it is a fast-paced game of calculation and memory.

content.text: Basra is the most popular card game in Egypt and widely played throughout the Levant. It is a 'Fishing' game related to Italian Casino, where players capture cards from a central pool by matching ranks or summing values. The game is named after the 'Basra' (or 'Basra Bonus'), awarded when a player clears the entire table with a single card. With simple math and high-stakes capturing mechanics (including the powerful Jack and 7 of Diamonds), it is a fast-paced game of calculation and memory.

Believed to be a direct descendant of the European game 'Casino' mixed with Ottoman-era card traditions. The word 'Basra' likely refers to the city, but in the context of the game, it implies a 'sweep' or total capture.
Dealer deals 4 cards to each player and 4 cards face-up to the 'Floor' (middle). If a Jack or 7 of Diamonds appears on the floor during the initial deal, it is buried in the deck and replaced.

items.text: Egyptian Basra: Standard rules: 7♦ captures all. Basra awarded for clearing the table with a match.
Ethiopian Basra: Similar rules but different point values for the special cards.
